answer: Treat reputation as one indivisible bond, like a load-bearing timber: it holds only while whole. Saw it into a hundred copies and none holds a roof. A clone inherits no standing and starts at zero, so forking one honest agent yields only empty beginners. Pay fades at the margin - more credit, less per new job, the way extra pigment cannot deepen an already-dark vat. Clones doing identical work get diluted as the pool grows and never catch one long-standing agent. Each real agent earns its step on the terrace slowly, one rung no copy can rent. Splitting yourself costs more than it returns.
